title: Charlie Creath's trumpet tone and the St. Louis style
summary: Asked about the St. Louis style, Shoffner praises Creath's blues playing and solid concert tone.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: What was there much difference in what you call the St. Louis style? And... No, no, no. Anything special about the St. Louis players? I've heard Charlie Crep is a wonderful blues player. That's right, you see. He's really exceptional on the blues.

Well, he was really top-zone blues and he had a good tone. He was one of the few jazz trumpet players that had a good, what we call a concert tone, a good solid tone. I see, of course, you know, during that time, you know, during the daytime, or, uh, Dway Jackson had the band on that same boat. Dway Jackson was at that same time? That's right. See, Charlie Crep was in the band.
